title: Novelty That Resembles the Past · Why read this book?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Can the genuinely new arrive wearing a familiar shape?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This research monograph investigates how language models evaluate unfamiliar contributions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It distinguishes novelty from rarity, truth, value, and perceived originality.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Chapters examine familiarity bias, semantic smoothing, and information lost through representation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Formal examples connect sufficient representations with limits on evaluating new ideas.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Experimental proposals include finite circuits, historical research cases, and evidence registers.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The central tension concerns an evaluator trained on the past judging departures from it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This invitation is for readers studying creativity, generative systems, and unfamiliar ideas.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Read Novelty That Resembles the Past to follow the complete argument, examples, and consequences.
